title: SpaceX and Tesla to Build $16.8 Billion Chip Plant in Texas, Creating 3,000 Jobs
excerpt: The Terafab facility in Grimes County will span 100 million square feet — making it the largest building on Earth — and produce AI chips for Tesla's Optimus robots, self-driving Cybercabs, and SpaceX's space-based data centers.
body:
• SpaceX and Tesla announced a $16.8 billion initial investment to build Terafab, a semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County, Texas
  • The 100-million-square-foot facility will be the world's largest building, producing AI chips for Tesla's robots and self-driving vehicles and SpaceX's orbital data centers
  • The plant will create at least 3,000 jobs, with Texas providing a $30 million Enterprise Fund grant and JETI program incentives
  • Total investment across all phases could reach $119 billion, with SpaceX and Tesla's combined chip demand expected to exceed current global supply

SpaceX and Tesla are building what they say will be the largest chip manufacturing facility on Earth — a $16.8 billion semiconductor plant in Grimes County, Texas, about 40 miles northwest of Houston.

The facility, dubbed Terafab, was announced on August 6 by SpaceX alongside Texas Governor Greg Abbott. It will span more than 100 million square feet of manufacturing space and consolidate chip design, fabrication, packaging, and testing under a single roof.

Scale and Purpose

Terafab is designed to address what SpaceX and Tesla describe as a looming gap between their combined chip demand and global supply. The two Elon Musk-led companies expect their semiconductor needs to exceed one terawatt of computing power annually — far beyond current global production capacity.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IBr13nHEfrA

"The Terafab is bringing cutting-edge manufacturing to America, creating thousands of high-paying jobs in the Lone Star State, and enabling us to produce AI chips at scale for use on Earth and in space."

— Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla

The chips produced at the facility will power Tesla's Optimus humanoid robots and self-driving Cybercabs, as well as high-performance processors designed for SpaceX's planned space-based data centers. Tesla described the Terafab as "the biggest chip manufacturing facility ever built."

"Both Tesla & SpaceX will need far more chips than current & future global production can supply," Tesla said in a post on X. The company emphasized that while it is "deeply appreciative" of current chip suppliers, the projected gulf between supply and demand made building their own facility a necessity.

Investment and Jobs

The $16.8 billion covers only the initial phase. A May filing from SpaceX estimated the total project cost could reach $119 billion across future expansion phases. The initial phase alone will create at least 3,000 jobs, with SpaceX saying 60% to 80% of new hires at its other Texas facilities have come from local residents — a pattern it expects to replicate in Grimes County.

Texas Governor Abbott extended a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant to SpaceX for the project. Terafab also qualifies for incentives under the Texas Jobs, Energy, Technology, and Innovation (JETI) program, created in 2023 to attract large-scale industrial projects.

"The first-of-its-kind Terafab facility will accelerate chip production in Texas at an unprecedented scale, create thousands of good-paying jobs in Grimes County, and expand economic opportunity for generations of Texans," Abbott said.

Site and Controversy

The facility will be built on the Gibbons Creek Reservoir, a body of water that once cooled a coal-fired power plant shut down in 2018. SpaceX said it plans to draw water from the reservoir rather than tap local groundwater, an attempt to preempt concerns about water use — a sensitive issue given the proliferation of data centers in Texas.

Not all residents are enthusiastic. Hundreds of Grimes County residents packed a county meeting the day before the announcement, raising concerns about millions of dollars in tax incentives and what they described as a lack of transparency in how the deals were structured.

Musk's Expanding Texas Footprint

Terafab deepens the connection between Musk's companies and Texas. SpaceX relocated its headquarters to Starbase, Texas, from California in 2024, citing the state's political environment. Tesla has been based in Austin since 2021, also having moved from California.

SpaceX said its Texas operations have generated more than $28 billion in economic impact and 56,000 direct and indirect jobs over the past two years. The company's existing Texas presence includes Starbase (launches), Bastrop (Starlink manufacturing), and McGregor (rocket testing).

Tesla broke ground in April on a research fab at its Giga Texas North Campus in Austin, which it described as a precursor to the Terafab project. The two companies have also been doing growing amounts of business with each other — SpaceX bought $329 million of Tesla Megapack battery products in the first half of 2026 alone.
